title: Role-and-authority matrix for bounded multi-agent reporting
author: Faye Niu
target_section: 2.6 Bounded multi-agent systems and human review
purpose: Define five bounded workflow roles through permitted inputs and tools, required typed outputs, explicit stop or failure conditions, and authorities each role must not exercise.

status.interpretation: Author synthesis of locally admitted literature and frozen project contracts; a conceptual authority boundary rather than an implementation or empirical result.

placement.purpose: Place LIT-T4 on one dedicated portrait page immediately after Section 2.6 and prevent Section 2.7 from preceding it when the exhibit is input at the approved chapter location.

inputs.role: Role, communication and orchestration design choices plus coordination and hallucination-propagation limits.
Programmed roles, tools, messages, control flow, termination and human-input conditions; pilot findings remain application-specific.
Design-science requirement to evaluate an artefact against stated objectives rather than infer utility from construction.
Independent assessment, uncertainty, testing, human oversight, documented limits and safe-failure controls.
Human-AI correction, dismissal, uncertainty, explanation, feedback and global-control design guidance.
Controlled-task evidence that interventions can reduce overreliance without establishing general team-performance or usability benefit.
Data, code, procedure, metric and reporting boundaries for repeatable evaluation.

row_traceability.authority_boundary: May propose a bounded plan and candidates; cannot admit evidence, create report claims, broaden permissions or publish.
May propose a typed extraction from admitted evidence and an exact locator; cannot repair gaps, decide support or approve.
Assesses and records support separately; cannot silently rewrite the producer output or seek replacement support.
Renders only eligible verified records and explicit exceptions; cannot introduce facts, alter verification or approve.
May approve, reject or return a version; cannot manufacture support or establish outcome benefit by presence alone.

limitations: The exhibit is an author synthesis and conceptual design contract, not an implementation or empirical result.
Role names, message exchange and separate records do not establish independent cognition, competence or collective intelligence.
The table does not claim that more agents, debate or role separation is universally superior to a simpler workflow.
The verifier records an assessment but cannot silently revise the producer output it is meant to assess.
The deterministic composer can render only eligible records and explicit exceptions; it cannot create or repair facts.
A named reviewer adds version-bound decision authority, not new evidence or proof of improved accuracy, trust, usability or utility.
AutoGen pilot results and Bucinca et al. controlled-task findings are not transferred to this artefact.
No unrun human-review outcome, live multi-agent performance, latency, token, cost or user-benefit value is reported.

outputs.role: One-page portrait LaTeX role-and-authority matrix with deterministic placement boundaries.
Complete plain-text alternative with expanded role, failure and authority boundaries.

self_hash_policy: The provenance file's own SHA-256 is reported externally because embedding it would create a self-referential hash.
